pr_title: drivers: fix and optimization of arc timer
pr_body:
For single core:
   the pulse triggered timer irq doesn't work for all targets. In
   iotdk, we found the clear of IP bit will clear int request
   when elapsed called in thread context. So come back to level
   triggered way, and use the sw triggered irq to remember the
   irq request which may be cleared in thread context with an
   exception that elapsed called in timer irq handler.

For SMP:
* still need to clear IP bit in timer irq handler

* last_time should be aligned to ticks, old code will miss some
  cycles, (curret_time - last_time) % CYC_PER_TICK

* in timeout set, the operations of timer aux regs require some cycles
  , use MIN_DELAY to guarantee this.

Code optimizations:
* rename overflow_cyc to overflow_cycles for better understanding
* use MIN macro to replace if .. else ..

Signed-off-by: Wayne Ren <wei.ren@synopsys.com>

Fixes #25178 
Fixes #25179
pr_comments: @vonhust will you address the review comments this week? This fixes to high-priority bugs so it's important that we get it merged.

> 1. May we have more precise explanation of what and why doesn't work on IoTDK as expected. Why do we see behavior which differs from other boards? Is that ARC EM version that has some (known?) specifics or it's ARC core configuration which leads to such a behavior? In any case I'd like to see a reference either to some documentation or bug-tracker entry which has a valid explanation of this phenomenon.
> 2. Please de-couple clean-up changes from real meat of this fix/change so we may focus on important changes.
> 3. Given yet another iteration of our timer driver rework maybe we start from design specification where we may capture known problems and explain how are we trying to get the ultimate implementation that just works? :)

I already split this PR into 3 commits.  For the root cause why iotdk doesn't work,  i think  it depends on how it configured in Architect.
@ruuddw  @abrodkin ,  now the sanitycheck tests of iotdk are clean.  Let's get it merged to fix the high priority issues, to not block the release of Zephyr.

review_comments: I'd suggest to move it to a separate change as well as it has nothing to do with the main reason for this patch - yet another subtle yet quite fundamental redesign of Timer IRQ handling for ARC.
Cannot we leave this variable rename out of this change? This hides important functional changes in between beautification changes.

I think it would be better to not call elapsed() in the timer ISR, but duplicate the relevant part of this code there. Makes things easier to understand and less complex (avoids this check that I can't oversee is always correct).

elapsed() may be called multiple in timer_int_handler, one is at the beginning,  others are called in z_clock_announce -> z_clock_set_timeout.

So better to handle it in elapsed()

Understood. Still, I'm not sure this solution is robust, e.g. if another interrupt handler calls elapsed() (reading the timer to get a timestamp for the input data).
And, I'd like to know why the pulse interrupts don't work on IoTDK.
